attempts.label: DANDI:001710
attempts.paper_title: Hippocampal place code plasticity in CA1 requires postsynaptic membrane fusion
attempts.entry_title: Place code plasticity after CA1 Stx3 deletion (Plitt, Kaganovsky et al. 2023)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's imaging and behavioral findings held in this data, a few did not, and several could not be tested. Cre mice licked less before the reward zone, place-code quality was unchanged, novelty-driven activity was lower in Cre mice, and reward cells were fewer. Narrower Cre fields held only partly, and the single-field and across-day backward shifts did not reproduce. Novelty preference and reward reversal could not be tested because those data are not deposited, and the synchronous-event and network-model findings were blocked by unspecified methods. All imaging results use dF/F, not the paper's deconvolved rates.
attempts.description: Tests the head-fixed imaging and virtual reality findings of Plitt, Kaganovsky, Sudhof and Giocomo (bioRxiv 2023) on dandiset 001710, which holds two-photon imaging of CA1 and VR behaviour of 9 control and 7 Cre mice over six days of a novel arm Y-maze. It compares anticipatory licking, novelty slowing, decoding, place fields, novelty-driven activity, reward coding, place field shifts and synchronous events between groups. The freely moving behaviour, the reward reversal days and the CA3 and dentate gyrus sessions are not in the dandiset.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds the head-fixed VR imaging of Ctrl-1 to Ctrl-9 and Cre-1 to Cre-7 on days 1 to 6. The freely moving T-maze, open field and elevated plus maze data (Fig 1B-C, S1), the reward reversal days 7 and 8 (Fig 5E-I), the Cre-8 CA2/3 and Cre-7 dentate gyrus sessions (Fig S5) and the morph task (Fig S4) are not in it, so 9 of the paper's findings cannot be tested.

The deconvolved activity rates that the preprint's Methods use for every imaging analysis are not deposited; the files hold dF/F, raw fluorescence and neuropil only, and the deconvolution kernel is not given.
The speed series ('Speed along Y maze', at imaging and full resolution) is labelled in 10 cm/s, but its integral over a trial is about 288 for the 300 cm track (median trial 10 s), so it is in cm/s.

The NWB files do not say which ROIs are the same cell across days. The authors' matches are on Figshare (doi 10.6084/m9.figshare.31286365.v5), indexed by a session order that is only in their code's mouse_metadata.py; with them, matched cells lie within 1 to 2 pixels after the field of view's shift.

The reward zone positions are not in the files or the dandiset metadata; the paper names them only as the beginning of the left arm and the end of the right arm. They were estimated from where rewards were given.

The dandiset also holds seven SparseKO mice (multiplexed two-channel files, SparseKO-4 without day 3), which are not in the preprint; the dandiset's name gives 2026 and its linked code describes a later version of the paper. Two days (Ctrl-2 day 4, Ctrl-4 day 2) are split over two files.
Fig 2B gives 17 familiar trials for Cre-3 on day 5; the file has 82 familiar trials (11 novel, 7 familiar in block 6). The other seven counts of Fig 2A-B match exactly.

The authors' code at commit f2ab24d takes the anticipatory window as the 5 bins before the zone front plus the front bin (behavior.py, rzone_ledge=5), where the Methods say 30 cm, and normalizes block-6 activity over the first 5 trials (novel_activity_rate.py, max_trial=5), where the Methods use the whole block. The code describes the later version of the paper.

Imaging and VR traces are consistent with a shared clock. The split-half reliability of familiar-trial maps peaks at zero shift for Ctrl-1 day 3 (0.962) and at -0.52 s for Cre-1 day 3 (0.956 against 0.953 at zero), falling at larger shifts in both directions; only these two days were checked.
The Methods give an imaging rate of 15.46 Hz; the 36 files of Ctrl-6 to Ctrl-9, Cre-6 and Cre-7 (the mice the Methods say were imaged at 920 nm) are at 15.51 Hz, the others at 15.46 Hz.

Question for the authors. Were the preprint's imaging figures made from deconvolved activity rates (which kernel and time constant) or from the dF/F deposited here, as the published code does? Every imaging outcome of this attempt uses the deposited dF/F.

Question for the authors. How is the population vector correlation defined (Fig 2G-H, S3B-C)? The flattened and the per-bin readings give different group results for the familiar to novel correlation (p=0.018 against p=0.31); the per-bin reading of the published code was adopted.

Question for the authors. In the HSE null, does the circular shift move a cell's whole activity series within the stopping period (so that transients that began before the stop can enter the null) or only the transients that began in the period? Which speed and smoothing define 'stationary (<2 cm/s)'? And how were HSEs told apart from chance coincidences? Read from the Methods, the detector flags, on data with synchrony removed (each cell shifted in time), 0.43 of Cre and 0.16 of control trials under the onset reading against 0.46 and 0.20 in the real data, and 0.15 against 0.26 of Cre trials under the series reading. The HSE claims are blocked for this. The Figshare shuffles (shuffle_pkls.zip) hold no HSE results.

Question for the authors. Where are the reward zones in spline coordinates, and how is the animal's average running speed taken for normalized speed (time-weighted or over bins)? The day-6 spatial pattern of vr-reward-location-learning holds for Cre mice only with the bin mean.

On the two days split over two files (Ctrl-2 day 4, Ctrl-4 day 2) the block numbers of the second file restart at 0, so the files alone give 5 and 4 blocks for those days; the authors' code continues them from the first file's last block, which gives 6 blocks with the novel trials in block 6.

Question for the authors. How were the deposited place-cell masks (place_cell_info) computed? They equal shuffle p < 0.05 of the deposited spatial information, but that information is on another scale than the Skaggs information of the trial-averaged dF/F map (recomputed over deposited, median 25 to 31), and a 1000-shuffle test recomputed here marks 0.1 to 49% more cells per mouse-day. The function that made them (two_photon_utils.spatial_analyses.place_cells_calc) is not in the linked repository.

entries.name: 001710-plitt-2023
entries.title: Place code plasticity after CA1 Stx3 deletion (Plitt, Kaganovsky et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the head-fixed imaging and virtual reality findings of Plitt, Kaganovsky, Sudhof and Giocomo (bioRxiv 2023) on dandiset 001710, which holds two-photon imaging of CA1 and VR behaviour of 9 control and 7 Cre mice over six days of a novel arm Y-maze. It compares anticipatory licking, novelty slowing, decoding, place fields, novelty-driven activity, reward coding, place field shifts and synchronous events between groups. The freely moving behaviour, the reward reversal days and the CA3 and dentate gyrus sessions are not in the dandiset.
